headline: Few people eligible for lung cancer screening discuss their risk with clinicians, CHEST findings show
dek: Findings presented at the CHEST annual meeting point to a communication gap that contributes to lung cancer screening lagging behind other cancer screening programmes.
body:
Lung cancer screening continues to lag behind screening for other types of cancer, in part because of a communication gap, according to findings presented at CHEST, the annual meeting of the American College of Chest Physicians. Few people who are eligible for screening are discussing their risk with clinicians, the findings indicate.

The work was presented in Phoenix on October 20, according to a post by Medscape on X.

Sarvesh Sharma, MD, a fellow of pulmonary disease and critical care medicine at Cape Fear Valley Medical Center and a clinical instructor at Methodist University Cape Fear Valley School of Medicine in Fayetteville, North Carolina, told attendees that addressing these deficits at multiple points along the screening continuum is essential to improve screening uptake and reduce mortality.

The post is a brief summary of a conference presentation. It did not give details such as study design, sample size or figures, and no peer-reviewed publication was cited.
